description: O11 (coverage of EDITING over STRUCTURE): change a composite type that this job did not create, and see what happens to whoever uses it as an output type and to the expressions that write its fields. The base is job:producer-public, so the public structure ProductSummary {Name Text, Price Currency}, the entity Product and the public server action Product_GetById (output Summary of type ProductSummary; Assign SetSummary writes Summary.Name and Summary.Price) already exist when the first op runs - there is no birth op here, on purpose: creating and editing in the same job proves no maintenance. Outside the job that created them there are no aliases: the structure is cited as 'IStructure:ProductSummary', an attribute as 'IStructure:ProductSummary/Name' and the action's parameter as 'IServerAction:Product_GetById/Summary'. The five changes are all on top of what the other job left written: add the attribute Sku (Text, with Description) to a structure that already had 2, change the DataType of Price (Currency -> Decimal) on an attribute that already existed, rename the attribute Name to Title WITH the inherited expression 'Summary.Name' writing it, rename the structure itself to ProductCard with 4 real consumers linked, and write the structure's Description. The central lesson is in the difference between the two renames: renaming the ATTRIBUTE rewrites by itself the expression that cites it (consumers 1, expressionsRewritten 1: 'Summary.Name' becomes 'Summary.Title'); renaming the TYPE rewrites nothing (consumers 4, expressionsRewritten 0), because no expression cites the name of the type - they cite the name of the PARAMETER (Summary) and of the attribute. Whoever holds the type holds it by KEY: the output Summary leaves the rename with the same DataType '@+svkyZ9luk2L1H3L5FngMg' and the anonymous record 'ProductSummary Record' becomes 'ProductCard Record' without a single op asking for it. Also measured: in O11 the get of an IStructureAttribute does NOT expose IndexInParent (the order is read from the dump and from the result of the move, see structure-refactor.json), and the Label of an attribute follows the rename because it is derived from the name. The refactor (move/duplicate/replace/delete) is in structure-refactor.json; the refusals are in tests/jobs-negative/delete-structure-attribute-in-use.json, delete-structure-in-use.json and rename-structure-clash.json.

ops.name: ProductSummary
ops._why: (0) starting point: the structure ALREADY exists before the first op of this job - it comes from job:producer-public. The find returns TWO objects with this name: the IStructure (OutSystems.Model.Data.IStructure, key +svkyZ9luk2L1H3L5FngMg) and the IAttribute 'ProductSummary' (OutSystems.Model.Types.IAttribute) of the anonymous record 'ProductSummary Record' that the platform generated with it. Keep the list: the find (13d) does it again after the rename of the structure and none of these names survives.

(1) BEFORE, the structure: Attributes 2, Fields 2, Public True, Description null, IsAnonymous False, TypeKind Element. Keep the ObjectKey +svkyZ9luk2L1H3L5FngMg: get (13f) must bring the same one, otherwise what followed was a re-creation and not an edit.

(2) BEFORE, the tree: 2 IStructureAttribute in birth order - Name (ohezZT4AgU+A7XHCWZLNgQ) and Price (4eTJh_j_GU2mlngZsUlJ7A), both OutSystems.Model.Data.IStructureAttribute. This is the snapshot that the dump (14) is compared against.

(3) BEFORE, the attribute that will be renamed: Name 'Name', Label 'Name' (derived from the name, nobody fixed it), DataType @uROOBXPvQEyU76NWO+1uxQ (Text), Description null. Note that there is NO IndexInParent in the properties of the get in O11 - the position in the sequence is only read in the dump or in the result of a move.
(4) BEFORE, the attribute that will change type: DataType @EYiTxdlAx0OG1Vuo4D_l4A (Currency), Decimals null, Length null. Compare with get (11b).

(5) BEFORE, the OUTPUT CONSUMER: the output Summary of the inherited action, with DataType '@+svkyZ9luk2L1H3L5FngMg' - the KEY of ProductSummary, not the name. Keep it: in get (13b) it must be the same, after the structure has changed its name.

(6) BEFORE, who holds the structure: count 4, real 4 - IOutputParameter Summary, IAttribute 'ProductSummary' of the anonymous record, and the two IExpression #Variable of the Assign ('Summary.Name' and 'Summary.Price'). None of those expressions cites the word 'ProductSummary': they cite the parameter Summary and the attribute. Keep that for the rename of the type, further down.

(7) BEFORE, who reads the attribute Name: count 1, real 1 - the IExpression '+Q5E_W6hzECEj71HiGgImQ.#Variable' with the text 'Summary.Name', in the Assign SetSummary. It is the one that the rename (12b) must rewrite by itself.

(8) BEFORE, who reads the attribute Price: count 1, real 1 - the IExpression 'vFxqteUZdUC4WBlsnq8m9w.#Variable' with the text 'Summary.Price'. Changing the type underneath this expression (11a) does not rewrite it; it is Verify that decides whether Currency -> Decimal is compatible with the Value 'GetProduct.List.Current.Product.Price'.
(9) BEFORE, the text in writing: the IAssignNode has two IAssignment, each with #Variable and #Value; the #Variable say 'Summary.Name' and 'Summary.Price'. The dump (12d) is read against this dump.

ops.name: Sku
ops._why: (10a) CHANGE 1 - add an attribute to the INHERITED structure. The parent is not an $alias: aliases are local to the job that declares them, and the one who declared this structure was another job; outside it the stable reference is 'IStructure:ProductSummary'. The object that is born is OutSystems.Model.Data.IStructureAttribute.
the Description of the new attribute, for the data contract to check back and for get (10b) to read.

(10b) AFTER: the new attribute, Name 'Sku', Label 'Sku', DataType @uROOBXPvQEyU76NWO+1uxQ (the same Text key as get 3), Description written, ParentStructure @+svkyZ9luk2L1H3L5FngMg. The alias $sku only exists because THIS job created it.

(10c) AFTER, the tree: 3 attributes where dump (2) showed 2 - Name, Price and Sku at the END of the sequence, not in the middle; the 2 inherited ones with the same keys. THE LESSON: the output Summary of the action just changed SHAPE without any op touching it - whoever has a composite type by contract inherits the contract that the type has at the moment.

(11a) CHANGE 2 - change the DataType of an attribute that ALREADY EXISTED, Currency -> Decimal, with the expression 'Summary.Price' alive, writing it from Product.Price (Currency). The change rewrites no text; Verify stays clean because Currency and Decimal are compatible in assignment. Changing to Text would be another experiment, and a negative one.

(11b) AFTER: compare with get (4). The DataType CHANGED (@EYiTxdlAx0OG1Vuo4D_l4A Currency -> @snOQIa2+VEi7MGyYOu7OpA Decimal); the Name, the Label, the ObjectKey 4eTJh_j_GU2mlngZsUlJ7A and the ParentStructure STAYED - the attribute did not change place or identity, only type.

ops.name: Title
ops._why: (12b) CHANGE 3 - rename an INHERITED attribute with a real consumer linked. The verb rename WORKS because IStructureAttribute publishes a writable Name. Measured: consumers 1, expressionsRewritten 1 - the only IExpression that cited it was rewritten. Read these counters, but do not deliver based on them: the proof is in the dump (12d).

(12c) AFTER: the path is now '/Title' (the old '/Name' no longer resolves), the ObjectKey is the SAME as get (3) (ohezZT4AgU+A7XHCWZLNgQ) and the Label followed along ('Title'), because it was derived from the name and nobody had fixed it by hand.

(12d) THE CENTRAL PROOF of this change: the #Variable of the first IAssignment now says 'Summary.Title' without a single fix by hand - the platform rewrote it. Only the LAST segment was rewritten: 'Summary' is still the output, because it was not renamed; the #Value 'GetProduct.List.Current.Product.Name' stayed intact, because it cites the attribute Name of the ENTITY Product, not the one of the structure. Compare word by word with the dump (9).

(12e) the same list as the usages (7): count 1, real 1, the SAME consumer key '+Q5E_W6hzECEj71HiGgImQ.#Variable' and the already rewritten text 'Summary.Title'. Changing the name did not move whoever uses it - the consumer is linked by key.

ops.name: Name
ops._why: (12f) the structure's attribute no longer answers to 'Name': what the list brings are the homonyms of the ENTITY Product (IEntityAttribute 'Name' and the IEntityAttributeSignature 'Name'), not the renamed attribute. The find is the right reading for this question: the counter of the rename says how many consumers there were, not whether the old name still exists somewhere.

ops.name: ProductCard
ops._why: (13a) CHANGE 4 - rename the INHERITED STRUCTURE itself, with 4 real consumers linked (output, anonymous record and two expressions). Measured: consumers 4, expressionsRewritten 0 - and it is the direct contrast with (12b): no expression cites the name of the type, so there is no text to rewrite, only keys that stay where they are.

(13b) AFTER, the output consumer: the DataType is the SAME key as get (5), '@+svkyZ9luk2L1H3L5FngMg', and the Digest of the parameter did not even change (Axmtftb6yOrGMgS9CgdIKg). The output is still called Summary - the name of the parameter is the choice of the action's author and does not follow the name of the type.

(13c) the consumers of the usages (6), with the SAME 4 keys and the same count (count 4, real 4): none broke and none was born. What changed in text was the path of the anonymous record, which became 'IAnonymousStructure:ProductCard Record/IAttribute:ProductCard' because its name is derived from the name of the type; the expressions still say 'Summary.Title' and 'Summary.Price'.

ops.name: ProductSummary
ops._why: (13d) EMPTY list: compare with the find (0), which returned TWO objects with this name. The IStructure and the IAttribute of the anonymous record followed the rename together, because the second is generated FROM the structure and is not author text.

ops.name: ProductCard
ops._why: (13e) and this is where the two reappear, with the new name and the SAME keys (+svkyZ9luk2L1H3L5FngMg and TIjBh2dnLkyRckxfDjbndw), without a single op asking for it. This pair of finds is the cheap proof that renaming a structure is more than swapping a label.

ops.value: Resumo de produto. Editado por structure-lifecycle.json.
ops._why: (13f') CHANGE 5 - write the Description of the structure, by the NEW name: the path 'IStructure:ProductSummary' no longer resolves. It is the write that the data contract checks back at the end.

(13f) AFTER, the structure: compare with get (1). The Name (ProductCard), Attributes/Fields (2 -> 3) and the Description (this job's, word for word) CHANGED; the ObjectKey +svkyZ9luk2L1H3L5FngMg, Public True and TypeKind Element STAYED. Five changes, zero rebuilds: the key is the same as in the first get.

(14) The final tree, to put beside the dump (2): the same object with another name, 3 attributes instead of 2, in the order Title (ohezZT4AgU+A7XHCWZLNgQ, the former Name), Price (4eTJh_j_GU2mlngZsUlJ7A, now Decimal) and Sku (R6GpKQcAP0uf13iBm0rhpA) at the end. The two inherited keys are those of the first dump. What the platform redid is all here (expression, Label, anonymous record); what was left for the author is here too (the Description).
